title: Rumble issued Tether shares and pre-funded warrants at the Northern Data closing

data.claim: Tether’s two-year $100 million Rumble advertising commitment remained a documented commercial relationship, but the fixed-price GPU customer agreement contemplated for the Northern Data transaction was not entered at closing. title: Pavlovski retained voting control despite Tether’s large pre-closing economic stake
summary: The April 2026 prospectus reported Chris Pavlovski at 34.8% economic ownership and 83.2% voting power, while Tether held 31.0% economic ownership and 7.4% voting power before completion of the exchange offer.

evidence.observation: The prospectus explicitly identifies Pavlovski—not Tether—as the controlling shareholder at the March 30, 2026 snapshot.

provenance.method: free-range five-role primary-source review and bounded graph synthesis

data.claim: At the March 30, 2026 pre-closing snapshot, Chris Pavlovski held 34.8% of Rumble economic ownership and 83.2% of voting power, while Tether held 31.0% economic ownership and 7.4% voting power. Tether’s large investment, contracts, lending, and warrants therefore should not be described as voting control without a post-closing analysis.

object.boundary: Pre-closing snapshot; post-closing fully diluted position unresolved.

data.adjudication: Pavlovski was the controlling voter at the stated snapshot; Tether had substantial economic and contractual exposure but not equivalent voting power.

title: Free-Range Batch 1 research pass, iteration 1
summary: Batch 1 revalidated four saturated targets without duplicating their graph and added the materially new RUM Group–Northern Data–Tether closing, securities, secured-credit, and control-boundary records.

evidence.observation: Foundation, Cabinet, EOP, and Cantor records were already structurally saturated; current official pages were used for time-bounded verification rather than duplicate entities.
June 2026 SEC filings added a new majority acquisition, legal-name change, securities issuance, secured-credit, collateral, and conversion-right surface around Rumble, Northern Data, and Tether.
Large economic, lender, and warrant exposure does not establish voting control; the latest pre-closing filing identifies Pavlovski as controlling voter.

provenance.method: free-range five-role primary-source review and bounded graph synthesis

data.research_question: What new primary-source facts or unresolved edges remain across the first Free-Range mission batch without duplicating already mature StarIntel records?
data.method: Five-role free-range cell: scout, archivist, verifier, linker, and skeptic; repository reuse check; official-source review; bounded synthesis.
classification_rules: Reuse existing canonical IDs and do not duplicate mature organization or person records.
Treat official website role pages as time-bounded snapshots.
Treat website navigation as non-exhaustive unless a source states completeness.
Separate economic ownership, voting power, creditor rights, warrants, commercial contracts, and operating control.
Do not infer a Donald Trump relationship from the Eddie and Jules Trump Foundation surname.

findings.finding: Current foundation pages continue to identify Eddy Shalev as chairperson and Eli Hurvitz as executive director; existing canonical governance records remain supported.
The White House Cabinet page continued to list Pulte and Sonderling in acting roles at retrieval.
The six-link EOP landing page is not an exhaustive legal roster when compared with the broader White House executive-branch description.
Cantor current materials identify a three-co-CEO structure and the post-Lutnick holding-company leadership transition.
Rumble acquired approximately 85.2% of Northern Data on June 17, 2026.
Tether received substantial shares and warrants and became secured lender to the Rumble Irish holding company.
The contemplated fixed-price GPU customer agreement was not entered at closing, while the advertising commitment remained a separate documented relationship.
The latest pre-closing ownership table identifies Pavlovski as controlling voter; post-closing fully diluted control remains unresolved.
